data.name: Shantanika
data.gender_notes: Shantanika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words 'Shanti' (peace) and 'Nika' (tranquility). The name Shantanika carries the meaning “Peaceful, Tranquil” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Shantanika usually hope their child will grow to embody peaceful, tranquil and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of inner peace and calmness.
data.etymology: Shantanika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Peaceful, Tranquil.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shantanika total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Shantanika' holds a profound cultural significance in Hinduism as it symbolizes inner peace and tranquility. It is believed that the name bestows upon the bearer a serene demeanor and a calm mind, qualities that are highly valued in Hindu culture and are associated with enlightenment and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Shantanika' holds a deep spiritual significance as it represents the soothing balm of inner peace and tranquility in a world full of chaos and turmoil. It is believed that by invoking the name, one can find solace from the stresses of daily life and connect with the divine within, leading to a more authentic and meaningful spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shantanika: Peaceful Goddess In Hinduism, the name Shantanika signifies the peaceful and tranquil nature of the Divine Goddess, bestowing her blessings upon the one bearing her name. The very sound of the name evokes serenity and calmness, instilling a sense of inner peace and harmony.

vedic_reference.note: शान्तिः (shāntiḥ) means peace, tranquility, and calmness in Sanskrit. The suffix निक (nika) is a common suffix for male names in Sanskrit.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Shantanika was the name of the daughter of King Shantanu and Queen Ganga in Hindu mythology. The name Shantanika carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
Another Shantanika was a princess of Magadha, who married Emperor Ashoka and bore him a son, Mahendra.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Shantanika' is derived from Sanskrit, where 'Shantana' means peaceful and 'Ika' means one. In modern contexts, this name is popular in various spheres. On Instagram, Shantanika is a popular handle for yoga instructors and practitioners. The account is filled with serene images and calming quotes, promoting a peaceful lifestyle. On Amazon, there's a book titled 'Shantanika: Stories of a Yogini', which narrates the life of a modern-day yogini, drawing inspiration from the ancient tradition. Lastly, on Goodreads, there are several books with the name Shantanika in the title, primarily focused on spiritual growth and self-discovery.

name_in_real_life.story: Anita Shantanika from Bangalore, India embodies the meaning of Shantanika - "Peaceful, Tranquil". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.
